svg.text: CHARGING IS THE MOST DANGEROUS OPERATION IN THE LIFE OF THIS MACHINE — OUTDOORS, TRAINED OPERATOR, NO IGNITION SOURCE
Complete every wetted joint. No threaded or elastomer joint remains.
Hydrostatic 21 bar, 5 min. Drain, dry with warm dry nitrogen.
Helium mass spectrometer under vacuum on the whole envelope.
200 C / 8 h at < 1 Pa through the charge tube, pumping throughout.
Let the bed reach ambient still under the pump. Do not vent.
Admit 4.9 kg anhydrous methanol by WEIGHT from a sealed burette.
Freeze-pump-thaw x3 on the receiver. Final pump to < 50 Pa at 0 C.
Cold-weld the charge tube, cut, then TIG cap the stub.
Helium bomb 3 bar / 4 h, then mass spectrometer.
One full solar cycle under observation. Record bed and receiver temperatures.
The cold trap protects the pump and, more importantly, stops methanol
vapour reaching the exhaust. Vent the pump outdoors, downwind.
Venting the envelope to air at any point after bake-out. Air in the bed is non-condensable gas and it never comes out again.
Charging by volume. Methanol expands 1.2 % per 10 K; the charge is a mass specification.
Any valve, gauge port or sight glass left on the wetted envelope. Every one is a leak path for the life of the machine.
Charging indoors, or anywhere without free ventilation and no ignition source within 5 m.
4.9 kg METHANOL / ONE-TIME PERMANENT CHARGE / NO FIELD SERVICE
